title: Budget-Efficient Automatic Algorithm Design via Code Graph

mechanism.domainTask: Budget-constrained LLM design of combinatorial optimization algorithms
mechanism.populationDetail: Many evaluated algorithms and unevaluated algorithm paths are maintained in a correction DAG; this is not a conventional bounded survivor pool.
mechanism.archiveDetail: The highest-fitness evaluated algorithm is retained as the reference for proposing corrections; the full evaluated set is also retained.
mechanism.replacementDetail: Algorithms are paths over a reusable code-correction DAG, not nodes in a candidate genealogy tree.
mechanism.generationDetail: The initial algorithm is sampled from scratch; subsequent candidates arise by applying localized add/replace/remove code corrections to compatible algorithm paths.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: A random forest predicts fitness from correction-incidence features to rank unevaluated paths; task fitness is still measured with the objective evaluator.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: The global best evaluated algorithm is the reference for proposing corrections; corrections can then be applied to multiple compatible paths.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: DAG-based reusable code corrections with correction-level Shapley credit assignment; algorithm paths compose toggled corrections.

provenance.sourcePdf: additional_papers/202605/Budget-Efficient Automatic Algorithm Design via Code Graph.pdf
provenance.citationWarning: Do not classify the correction DAG as a genealogy tree or correction composition as multi-parent fusion. The fixed 50/50 candidate-evaluation split is distinct from generation-operator selection.
